equations.label: L1
equations.section: A Structural Law of Epistemic Environments
equations.text: When the external generation of coherent structure increases without bound, observable production ceases to serve as a unique indicator of internal organization.
equations.meaning: The paper's central structural law: under unlimited generative availability, externally supplied structure becomes empirically equivalent to (observationally indistinguishable from) internally constructed structure, so production stops uniquely indexing understanding.

equations.label: L2
equations.meaning: The structural regime shift: once generative availability exceeds a system's current discriminative capacity, accumulation collapses as a reliable path to competence and only selective retention/active stabilization (discrimination) preserves long-term coherence; the transition is environmentally driven, not ideologically chosen.
